original.target_description: Original Farris et al. (2008) study: participant gender main effect in the GLM predicting positive-affect perceptual sensitivity to friendliness versus sexual interest; Results paragraph following Table 1.

n.sample_role: Participants in the positive-affect sensitivity GLM; critical-model analytic sample size not explicitly stated.
n.exclusions: No critical-model exclusion or missing-data count is documented in the supplied Method, Statistical Analysis, or Results sections.
n.location: Method: Participants and Analysis; Statistical Analysis; Results, positive-affect sensitivity paragraph immediately after Table 1.
n.quote: Two hundred eighty heterosexual undergraduate men (63.6%) and women (36.4%) participated in exchange for course credit. ... Choice-model parameters, sensitivity and bias, were estimated for each participant individually ... Compared with women (ln(α) = 2.30), men (ln(α) = 1.61) were significantly less sensitive to the distinction between friendliness and sexual interest, F (1, 278) = 123.38, p < .001, η p 2 = .326.

notes: Only n_o is assigned. Source title, authors, year, and DOI match the original reference. The target is the gender main effect for positive-affect sensitivity, rather than classification-error t tests, negative-affect sensitivity, or decisional bias. The Participants section reports 280 study participants, and parameters were estimated individually, but no explicit analytic N or mutually exclusive final group counts are given for this critical GLM. The recruitment total is retained only as a candidate and is not promoted to analytic N; no N is inferred from F degrees of freedom. No arithmetic performed. No PDF was supplied. Other side/fields are unassigned placeholders.
